questions.question: Which of the following structures is listed as a content of the axilla?
questions.explanation: The contents of the axilla include the axillary artery, axillary vein, cords of the brachial plexus, axillary lymph nodes, fibrofatty tissue, axillary tail of breast, and the long thoracic and intercostobrachial nerves.

questions.question: The axillary artery is the main artery of which part of the body?
questions.explanation: The axillary artery is explicitly described as the main artery of the upper limb.

questions.question: Where does the axillary artery begin?
options: At the lower border of the teres major
At the outer border of the first rib
At the inner border of the second rib
At the lower border of the pectoralis minor
questions.explanation: The axillary artery begins at the outer border of the first rib as the continuation of the subclavian artery.

questions.question: The axillary artery ends by becoming which artery?
questions.explanation: It ends by becoming the brachial artery at the lower border of the teres major.

questions.question: Which muscle crosses the axillary artery on its superficial aspect to divide it into three parts?
questions.explanation: The pectoralis minor muscle crosses the axillary artery on its superficial aspect, dividing it into three parts.

questions.question: In the axilla, the axillary artery runs from its apex to the base along the lateral wall, nearer to which wall?
questions.explanation: The artery runs from its apex to the base along the lateral wall, nearer to the anterior wall than the posterior wall.

questions.question: The first part of the axillary artery is located in which position relative to the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: The first part is superior (or proximal) to the muscle.

questions.question: The second part of the axillary artery is located in which position relative to the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: The second part is posterior (or deep) to the muscle.

questions.question: The third part of the axillary artery is located in which position relative to the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: The third part is inferior (or distal) to the muscle.

questions.question: Which structure lies medial to the axillary artery throughout its course?
questions.explanation: The axillary vein lies medial to the axillary artery throughout its course.

questions.question: In the relations of the first part of the axillary artery, which nerve is located posteriorly?
questions.explanation: The posterior relations of the first part include the medial cord of the brachial plexus, long thoracic nerve, and serratus anterior (first digitation).

questions.question: Which cord of the brachial plexus lies laterally to the second part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The lateral cord of the brachial plexus is the lateral relation of the second part of the axillary artery.

questions.question: Which structure is a medial relation of the third part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The medial relations of the third part include the axillary vein, medial cutaneous nerve of forearm, and ulnar nerve.

questions.question: How many branches does the axillary artery give from its first part?
questions.explanation: The axillary artery gives one branch from the first part, two from the second part, and three from the third part.

questions.question: The superior thoracic artery arises from which part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The superior thoracic artery arises from the first part of the axillary artery.

questions.question: The thoraco-acromial artery emerges at which border of the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: The thoraco-acromial artery emerges at the upper border of the pectoralis minor.

questions.question: The thoraco-acromial artery pierces which fascia?
questions.explanation: It pierces the clavipectoral fascia and soon breaks up into four branches.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a branch of the thoraco-acromial artery?
questions.explanation: The four branches are pectoral, deltoid, acromial, and clavicular. The subscapular artery is a separate branch from the third part of the axillary artery.

questions.question: The lateral thoracic artery runs along which border of the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: The lateral thoracic artery emerges at and runs along the inferior border of the pectoralis minor.

questions.question: Which artery is the largest branch of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The subscapular artery is described as the largest branch of the axillary artery.

questions.question: The circumflex scapular artery is a branch of which artery?
questions.explanation: The circumflex scapular artery is a large branch of the subscapular artery.

questions.question: The posterior circumflex humeral artery passes through which space?
questions.explanation: It passes backwards, along with the axillary nerve, through the quadrangular intermuscular space.

questions.question: The anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries anastomose to form an arterial circle around which structure?
questions.explanation: They form an arterial circle around the surgical neck of the humerus.

questions.question: The arterial anastomosis around the scapula is formed between branches of the subclavian artery and which other artery?
questions.explanation: The scapular anastomosis is principally formed between branches of the first part of the subclavian and the third part of the axillary arteries.

questions.question: Which artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk that participates in the scapular anastomosis?
questions.explanation: The suprascapular artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk from the first part of the subclavian artery.

questions.question: The acromial branch of which artery anastomoses over the acromion process?
questions.explanation: The acromial branch of the thoraco-acromial artery anastomoses over the acromion with branches of the suprascapular and posterior circumflex humeral arteries.

questions.question: Clinically, what does the scapular anastomosis provide if the subclavian or axillary arteries are blocked?
options: Direct blood supply to the heart
questions.explanation: It serves as a potential pathway (collateral circulation) to ensure adequate circulation to the upper limb if the main arteries are blocked.

questions.question: The neurovascular structures in the axilla are protected by the arm on the side of the body and what other cushioning matrix?
questions.explanation: They are protected by the arm and the cushioning matrix, which is the axillary fat (fibrofatty tissue).

questions.question: Which structure is vulnerable to injury when the arm is abducted?
questions.explanation: The neurovascular structures are vulnerable to injury when the arm is abducted.

questions.question: The clavicular branch of the thoraco-acromial artery supplies which structure?
questions.explanation: The clavicular branch supplies the sternoclavicular joint.
